messages.subject: Re: NaN from ADREPORT for simple model
messages.subject_clean: NaN from ADREPORT for simple model
messages.body_plain:
After discussions with Jim Thorson, he identified where the problem is by trying different methods of how the Hessian is calculated. Turns out inside sderport it's using optimHess which uses finite differences. Here's a test:

# Works (using TMB automatic-differentiation hessian
SD = sdreport( Obj, hessian.fixed=Obj$he(Opt$par) )

# Fails using optimHess for finite-difference hessian using function and gradient
Hess = optimHess(Opt$par, fn=Obj$fn, gr=Obj$gr)
SD = sdreport( Obj, hessian.fixed=Hess )

# Fails using optimHess for finite-difference hessian using function only
Hess = optimHess(Opt$par, fn=Obj$fn )
SD = sdreport( Obj, hessian.fixed=Hess )

# Also fails using finite-difference hessian
sqrt(diag(solve(Hess)))

# Works using different finite-difference method
Hess = numDeriv::hessian( func=Obj$fn, x=Opt$par )
SD = sdreport( Obj, hessian.fixed=Hess )

Maybe someone has ideas on how to use the AD obj$he function within sdreport (where possible)? Or other general ideas on how to improve it.

As far as I can tell the core issue is the difference in magnitudes of the SEs of the two parameters. If I divide the covariate by 1000 (or standardize it) the model runs just fine.

On Thursday, December 28, 2017 at 6:51:28 PM UTC-3, Cole Monnahan (mon...@uw.edu) wrote:
>
> I’m trying to recreate a simple Poisson GLM (intercept and slope, no random effects) and running into a strange issue. When I fit the model nlminb returns convergence of 1 (false convergence (8)) despite having good gradients. If I do
> sqrt(diag(solve(Obj$he())))
>
> I get the same SEs as the glm function. However, when I run sdreport, with ADREPORT only for the two paramters, I get:
> Warning message:
> In sqrt(diag(cov)) : NaNs produced
>
> and then it returns
> sdreport(.) result
>            Estimate Std. Error
> beta0  4.3164849854        NaN
> beta  -0.0001058506        NaN
> Warning:
> Hessian of fixed effects was not positive definite.
> Maximum gradient component: 0.0002560145
> Warning message:
> In sqrt(diag(object$cov.fixed)) : NaNs produced
>
> I’m confused because previously it was able to invert obj$he(). I don’t need to use ADREPORT variables here, obviously, but I’m confused why this would occur. Why would I be able to invert the Hessian directly but sdreport cannot? Further, if I centered the covariate associated with the slope, then TMB fits and both methods work and match the glm function.
>
> I can post the data/model if it helps.
>
> Thanks,
> Cole
> ​
